judge: Priya — WCAG 2.2 AA auditor (screen-reader and keyboard-only usability sessions)
first_five_minutes:
Cassy lands on Mission Control. It is beautiful and it reads as hers: "Good afternoon, Cassandra.", "Your call, every time.", six DEMO-badged metrics, "Nothing leaves without you." Nothing lies to her — the agent panel literally says "Not running. Not pretending to." (agent-status.tsx:19). She tabs: the skip link appears properly (globals.css:1929-1940), focus rings are a clear gold 2px at 4px offset (globals.css:100-103), the sidebar reads as a real nav with descriptions. So far this is a careful, adult product. Then she goes to her Desk to try the thing the app is actually for: writing down an idea. And the first friction is visual, not conceptual — she cannot see where the fields are. "Give it a title" and "Your idea" are boxes whose only boundary is a 1px #37382f line at 1.57:1 against the page (globals.css:26, input.tsx:10); the fill is 1.11:1. On the desktop screenshot the inputs read as faint rectangles you locate by the placeholder text, not by the field. She'll find them; someone with low vision on a laptop in a bright room will hunt. Same story for the most consequential control in the whole product — the manuscript permission checkbox (globals.css:3602, library.css:22), a 20px box with a 1.57:1 border. That is a 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast failure, and it is systemic: every input, textarea, select and checkbox in the app. Second, the reading. A very large share of the copy that carries meaning — provenance badges, "Not saved yet · Kept in this tab", every eyebrow, every nav description, every error message — runs at 11px (globals.css:32, 1799), and a few load-bearing labels run lower: "Manuscript-supported · unreviewed" vs "Interpretation · verify with source" at 10px (library.css:90), the evidence Source ID at 10px (evidence-drawer.tsx:58), the sidebar section labels at 9–10px (globals.css:250, 286, 365, 422). The most important honesty signals in the product are set in the smallest type in the product. Third, if she were using a screen reader she would miss most of the app's reassurance. The pattern the codebase uses nine times — mount a `

` at the same moment as its text — does not announce in NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver: "That brief is not available in your workspace" (desk-page.tsx:82), "Opening your saved workspace…" (connected-home.tsx:102), "Your question is being saved and considered" (studio-page.tsx:198), "Loading your saved plans…" (plans-page.tsx:53), "Opening your book library…" (connected-library.tsx:68). The forms that got this right — manual-review-form.tsx:258, studio-page.tsx:217, learn-page.tsx:195, access-page.tsx:126 — prove the team knows the correct pattern; it just isn't applied consistently. She would still finish her first idea, and the save-state honesty ("Not saved yet · Kept in this tab until you save.", manual-review-form.tsx:248) would land. The bones are good. The finish is not AA.

scores.verdict: Consent is genuinely well-designed at the moment of asking — spoilers default off, manuscript permission is explicit, draft-conflict dialogs never overwrite without a choice, reading can be paused. But two real gaps remain: she cannot take her manuscript back, and as an Editor she cannot get her own marketing plan's tasks dated without the Owner. One control also commits before she confirms.

scores.verdict: Draft protection is the strongest thing in this codebase — the session-ended dialog hands back every unsaved word with a copy button, the corrupt-workspace dialog offers a download before anything is replaced, edits are keyed to the draft version they were written against. Two holes: one destructive action has no confirmation and no undo, and one control saves on keystroke.

scores.verdict: The app explains itself unusually well in prose — provenance labels, save-state, 'Reading is a separate step that you start', the manuscript consent list. What undermines it is that several machine-facing strings leak straight into the UI, and most loading/empty state announcements never reach a screen reader.

scores.verdict: The fundamentals are handled with real care — skip link, reduced-motion block, 16px inputs and 44px targets on mobile, lucide icons auto-hidden, dialog focus return, aria-errormessage on the main forms, clean heading order, labelled progress. But I found a systemic 1.4.11 failure across every form control, an aria-live pattern that does not announce repeated in nine files, a live region wrapping an entire results list, a select that commits on arrow-key, and focus that jumps backwards after every access change. An axe pass cannot see any of these.

top_findings.title: Every form control fails WCAG 1.4.11: input/select/checkbox borders are 1.4–1.6:1
top_findings.problem: `--input: #37382f` gives a 1.57:1 boundary against the #121312 page and 1.41:1 against the control's own #1d1e1b fill; `--border: #33342c` (line 25) is 1.48:1 and bounds every native select (globals.css:3406). The custom checkbox (globals.css:3602, library.css:22) inherits the same 1.5px #37382f outline. Non-text Contrast requires 3:1 for the visual information needed to identify a UI component. This affects the desk idea form, plan forms, access forms, login, connections, the studio question box and — most consequentially — the manuscript permission checkbox.
top_findings.proposed_change: Set `--input: #6f7264` (4.0:1) and introduce a separate `--hairline: #33342c` for decorative separators, leaving `--border` at a 3:1-or-better value wherever it draws a control boundary. Verify the rendered borders on /desk, /plans, /access and the manuscript upload panel.

top_findings.title: Nine status messages never announce: live regions are mounted together with their text
top_findings.problem:
The codebase repeatedly renders `{condition &&

…

}`. Inserting an aria-live container and its content in the same commit does not trigger announcement in NVDA, JAWS or VoiceOver. Affected: desk-page.tsx:82, connected-home.tsx:102, studio-page.tsx:198 and 204, plans-page.tsx:53/121/122, connected-library.tsx:68, opportunities-page.tsx:20, connected-book-detail.tsx:133 and 173. A screen-reader user gets no loading, no empty-state and no 'your question is being saved' feedback on those screens.
top_findings.proposed_change:
Convert each to an always-mounted region whose text toggles, e.g. `

{message}

` with `message` defaulting to `""` and a `:empty { display:none }` rule (the pattern already used at manual-review-form.tsx:258, studio-page.tsx:217, learn-page.tsx:195, access-page.tsx:126 and globals.css:3417).

top_findings.title: Manuscript upload errors render outside the form and cannot be heard
top_findings.problem:
`{error &&

}` sits after the upload Card and after the 'Bring a business question' Card, so the result of the most sensitive action in the product appears far from the control that caused it, is mounted with its text (so it does not announce), and focus is never moved to it. Compounding this, `required` on the file input and the permission checkbox (line 142, 148) means the hand-written messages at lines 103-104 can never fire.
top_findings.proposed_change: Move the error and success paragraphs inside the upload `<form>` above the submit button, keep both always mounted with empty text, drop `required` in favour of the existing custom checks, wire `aria-invalid`/`aria-errormessage` on the file input and checkbox to the error paragraph's id, and focus the error on failure (manual-review-form.tsx:85 pattern).

top_findings.title: Plan task status commits on every select change (WCAG 3.2.2)
top_findings.problem: `onChange={e=>void act({action:"task", …, status:e.target.value})}` writes to the server the instant the select value changes. On Windows, a keyboard user arrowing through a closed native select fires change on every option passed, so 'To do' → 'Done' → 'Skipped' all get saved. There is no confirmation, no announcement and no undo.
top_findings.proposed_change: Hold the value in local state and add an explicit 'Save progress' button per task (mirroring 'Save role' at access-page.tsx:150), or commit only on blur/Enter; announce the saved status in the page's always-mounted status region.

top_findings.title: Search results list is wrapped in role="status"
top_findings.problem: `<div role="status" className="library-search-results">` contains the count, every result excerpt, every location eyebrow and a 'Show full passage' button per result. When results change, the entire set — including button labels — is announced. With ten matches this is a wall of speech a user cannot interrupt meaningfully.
top_findings.proposed_change: Put `role="status"` on a small dedicated paragraph holding only the count sentence, and render the result cards in a plain sibling container.

top_findings.title: Meaningful text below 12px, including the provenance labels the product depends on
top_findings.problem: `.knowledge-proof` is 10px — that is the 'Manuscript-supported · unreviewed' vs 'Interpretation · verify with source' distinction. `.knowledge-index small:last-child` is 10px. The evidence Source ID is `text-[10px]` (evidence-drawer.tsx:58). `--text-xs: 11px` (globals.css:32) drives all eyebrows, nav descriptions, save-state, DEMO/MANUAL SNAPSHOT badges (globals.css:565) and error messages (globals.css:1799). Sidebar labels run 9–10px (globals.css:250, 286, 365, 422, 451). The cover text at 7–9px is correctly `aria-hidden` (book-card.tsx:15) and is not a concern.
top_findings.proposed_change: Raise `--text-xs` to 12px and `--text-sm` to 13px; move the ~40 hardcoded `font-size: 11px` rules onto the token; raise `.knowledge-proof`, `.knowledge-index small:last-child` and the evidence Source ID to 12px.

top_findings.title: Focus jumps backwards above the member list after every access change
top_findings.problem: `requestAnimationFrame(() => (focusAlert.current ? alertRef : statusRef).current?.focus())` runs after every request, including success. The status paragraph at line 126 is above the access grid, so after saving a role or granting access the keyboard user is dropped above the list and must Tab through it again. Focusing an aria-live element also produces a double announcement in JAWS.
top_findings.proposed_change: On success, leave focus on the invoking button and let the always-mounted status region announce; keep the focus move only for the error branch.

top_findings.title: A saved connection link is deleted by a single icon button with no confirm and no undo
top_findings.problem: The Trash2 icon button calls `change("DELETE", …)` directly. It is a Tab stop with the accessible name 'Remove My author profile' and no confirmation step, in an app where sign-out, demo reset, member removal and draft replacement are all confirmed. Focus after removal is also lost when the list re-renders.
top_findings.proposed_change: Route through a confirmation Dialog naming the link and stating that nothing on the platform changes, then return focus to the list heading or the next remove button.

top_findings.title: No way to take a manuscript back
top_findings.problem: 'Removing a manuscript from the app isn’t available yet — ask your workspace owner if you need a file removed' (repeated at line 170). The disclosure is honest, which is why it scores so well on trust, but the capability gap is the biggest agency and creative-respect gap in the product: her most intimate file is one-way once uploaded.
top_findings.proposed_change: Ship a 'Request removal of this version' action that files an owner-addressed desk brief with the manuscript id and version, and state what removal will and will not erase. Actual deletion (storage object, chunks, embeddings, audit row) is an owner decision and a SQL migration, not a tonight fix.
top_findings.owner_decision_needed: Whether and how manuscripts can be deleted — retention policy, what happens to derived knowledge and citations, and who may trigger it. Code can ship the request path tonight; the deletion itself needs the owner's call and a migration.

top_findings.title: Owner review gates the author's own marketing plan
top_findings.problem: As an Editor, Cassy can build and generate a plan for her own books but cannot activate dated tasks; the screen explains the gate warmly but offers only a link to /access. In a product whose thesis is 'the call is yours', the one place a plan becomes actionable is the one place she needs Michael.
top_findings.proposed_change: Owner decision on the right; in code, at minimum add an in-page 'Ask for a review' action that records the request and shows its state, so she can move the plan forward from here rather than leaving the screen.
top_findings.owner_decision_needed: Whether an Editor may approve and activate her own plans, or whether owner review stays. If it stays, whether a request-review action is acceptable given the no-notification rule.

what_works: Reduced motion is handled properly: `html { scroll-behavior: smooth }` (globals.css:68) is neutralised along with all animation and transition durations under `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` (globals.css:2620-2627), and the `.animate-spin` refresh icon on /raven is covered by it.

iOS zoom-on-focus is prevented deliberately: `body :is(input, textarea, select)…{ font-size: 16px }` inside the 760px breakpoint (globals.css:3588), alongside `min-height: 44px` for inputs, selects and every `[data-slot="button"]` (globals.css:3589-3596). Desktop targets are all ≥24×24, so SC 2.5.8 is met.

Decorative iconography is genuinely silent: lucide-react v1.47 emits `aria-hidden="true"` whenever no a11y prop is passed (node_modules/lucide-react/dist/cjs/lucide-react.js:64-66), and the one place with real text inside a decorative graphic — the placeholder book cover — is explicitly `aria-hidden` (book-card.tsx:15) with the title repeated in the `<h3>`.

The best-practice live-region pattern does exist here and is worth copying everywhere: always-mounted, empty by default, hidden via `:empty { display: none }` — manual-review-form.tsx:258, studio-page.tsx:217, learn-page.tsx:195, access-page.tsx:126 and globals.css:3417.

Polling does not spam the screen reader: the manuscript reading announcement is throttled to one sentence per state change or once per 20 seconds (connected-book-detail.tsx:51-57) into a stable region (line 153), and the `<progress>` element carries both `aria-label` and `aria-valuetext`.

Dialog focus is managed by hand where the default would be wrong: the sign-out confirmation focuses 'Keep working' on open and returns to the sign-out button on close (app-shell.tsx:472-473); approve/reject dialogs focus Cancel first and return to the trigger, falling back to the Reviewed tab when the trigger has unmounted (approval-card.tsx:197-205).

Error handling on the main forms is textbook: `aria-required`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-errormessage` pointing at a `role="alert"` paragraph that is then focused — manual-review-form.tsx:190-192/240, plans-page.tsx:74-75/87/136-138, studio-page.tsx:192.

Character counting is done right: the visible '0 / 10,000' is `aria-hidden` and a separate `sr-only` string gives graded, non-chatty feedback only near and at the limit (manual-review-form.tsx:203-214).

Heading structure is clean across every page I read — one `h1` per route, `h2` per card/section, `h3`/`h4` nested correctly inside the knowledge workbench (book-knowledge.tsx:88, 91, 101) and the studio result (studio-page.tsx:205-208).

Status is never conveyed by colour alone: the creative-firewall list pairs a check/cross icon with the words 'Allowed'/'Prohibited' (settings-page.tsx:80-83), and metric cards carry an `sr-only` detail sentence including 'Demo data' (metric-card.tsx:42).

The skip link is real and visible on focus (globals.css:1929-1940, app-shell.tsx:363), `<main id="main-content" tabIndex={-1}>` is a valid target, and the permission-retry flow returns focus there deliberately (workspace-permission-notice.tsx:12).

External links consistently announce themselves: ` (opens in a new tab)` on connections-page.tsx:99/130 and setup-status.tsx:63/74, and a full `aria-label` on the daily quote source (daily-quote.tsx:12).
Toasts have no auto-dismiss timer anywhere in lib/db/demo-store.tsx, so SC 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable is not engaged — a notice waits until she dismisses it.

The inspiration carousel is a correctly built one: `aria-roledescription="carousel"`, an `sr-only` keyboard-help string wired via `aria-describedby`, arrow/Home/End handling that defers to inner links and buttons, and a polite position region that also speaks the new idea's title (inspiration-shelf.tsx:49-62).
